source.prompt: Generate exactly ONE complete game-ready basketball player from this single front-view T-pose reference. The input contains one person. Create one body only: no duplicates, extra figures, turnaround board. Preserve the character’s dark brown skin, short black hair, lean long-limbed athletic build, broad shoulders, large hands, and oversized high-top shoes. Use connected natural anatomy with clean shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles. Keep a symmetrical T-pose with straight horizontal arms, palms down, separated fingers, straight legs, and parallel feet. Match the original fictional uniform: deep muted-purple loose jersey and baggy knee-length shorts, cream piping, cream angular side panels, small broken-square chest emblem, and cream number 07. Use cream socks and chunky cream shoes with purple panels and dark soles. Style it like a 2004 PS2 basketball-game player: smooth-shaded economical geometry, strong readable silhouette.

Adapt T-pose hand orientation and ball anchors; use candidate-specific reachable idle and finish targets.
Export selected mesh and rig only from live Blender; retain raw and working files outside runtime assets.

validation.notes: First movement/possessed-dribble experiment only, selected with ?animation=hybrid. Whole-player CPU includes procedural fallback update, skeletal pose, and final contact solve. Desktop 1280×800; actual coarse-pointer touch emulation at 320×568, 390×844, 844×390; real browser input and cancellation tested. Plant metrics cover steady fully planted portions, not deliberate release/turn transitions. Contact point follows top of authoritative game ball only in declared apex window. One source stride remains fast at game walk/sprint speeds; lateral/pivot fidelity, finger shape, contact blending outside apex, and physical-device/multiplayer performance remain limitations.
